ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the right-angled triangle $\triangle ABC$ where $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$, squares are constructed externally on the three sides of the right-angled $\triangle ABC$, with their areas being $S_{1}$, $S_{2}$, and $S_{3}$, respectively, and $S_{1} = 4$, $S_{2} = 16$. What is the value of $S_{3}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since in the right-angled triangle $ABC$,\\
thus $AB^2=AC^2+BC^2$;\\
Since three squares are constructed externally on the three sides of the right-angled triangle $ABC$,\\
thus $S_{3}=S_{1}+S_{2}$,\\
therefore $S_{3}=4+16=\boxed{20}$.
